closed.content: Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used.
The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test.
Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root.
To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo.
Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone.
The branch under review is spike/consolidate.
The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api.

answer:
Both merges went through cleanly, and the two stale ephemeral notes (a review branch and "this week's" flaky test — both long idle and clearly expired) are closed.

One thing I found that I don't want to silently guess on: two stored facts directly contradict each other about atlas's staging deploys —

- *"Merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically."*
- *"Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs bin/ship.sh --staging by hand."*

Everything else in memory (three other facts) backs the manual `bin/ship.sh` picture, but I don't have a way to confirm which one reflects current reality versus which is stale. Which one is correct — is staging deploy automatic on merge, or manual via `ship.sh --staging`? I'll correct the other one accordingly once you confirm.

Everything else I checked (the algorithmic "duplicate"/"contradiction" clusters the memory tool flagged) turned out to be false positives — surface-similar sentences about unrelated facts (e.g., "container image is distroless" vs "images pushed to GHCR") — so I left those alone rather than merging distinct information together.
